body.text: Monsieur. I write in the plainest English I have, which is not much, so that there is no mistaking it.
Your settlement at {param:town} grows. I have counted the roofs from the water twice this year and there are more of them each time. This is admirable in you and inconvenient for me.
I should like {param:amount}, in coin. It is not a trade; I have nothing to offer you and I would not insult you by pretending otherwise.
My frigates winter badly and their officers grow quarrelsome. I say this as a man describing his own difficulties, not yours.
I shall not mention the matter to your Crown. Neither, I imagine, will you.

tone.text: To the Lieutenant-General of the Leeward Isles — I write {choice}.

options.label: pay him
options.text: The sum will be sent from my Treasury. I trust your season improves.

options.label: refuse him
options.text: You will have nothing from me, this season or any other.
